claims: As of April 2026, the USPS is temporarily suspending contributions to its employee pension plans (FERS).
The USPS's temporary suspension of contributions to its employee pension plans (FERS) is to manage a "pending liquidity crisis".
The USPS's temporary suspension of contributions to its employee pension plans (FERS) affects roughly $400 million in monthly payments.
USPS employees primarily participate in the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS).
FERS includes a defined benefit pension, Social Security, and the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP).
FERS is the primary plan for most employees hired after 1984.
CSRS (Civil Service Retirement System) is an older system covering employees hired before 1984.
Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) is a defined contribution plan similar to a 401(k).
USPS matches contributions to Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) up to 5% of pay.
Pension benefits are calculated based on years of service and the average of the highest three consecutive years of salary ("high-3").
USPS announced in April 2026 that it is pausing employer payments to the pension fund.
USPS is pausing employer payments to the pension fund due to financial constraints.
USPS is pausing employer payments to the pension fund to conserve cash.
